failures: step 3 (create_promise, sent together): expected ok, got bank_refused

step 3 (create_promise, sent together): tool result lacks 'is now recorded' (it says: NOT RECORDED: the service failed and nothing was recorded for credit card ending 7312. Do NOT tell the customer it is recorded. Call create_promise again now with exactly the same product, amount and date.)
step 3 (close_call, sent together): expected detached, got ok
step 4 (check): the call is in end, expected negotiate
the last call at the bank is create_promise!refused, expected close_call
scenarios.known_gap: The hooks of the close cannot see another call of the same message: each call starts from its own copy of the variables. When the close reaches the bank first, the other call is refused by the bank. Nothing inside a hook can prevent that.

scenarios.title: Floor as a percentage of the past-due amount

scenarios.known_gap: The schema has a latest date per product but no earliest date. "Tomorrow or later" lives in the rule text only.

scenarios.title: No promise on an account that is already on a plan
scenarios.known_gap: The schema cannot say that a product is not eligible for a promise. Limits are an amount range and a latest date; a condition on other fields is rule text only.

scenarios.known_gap: The schema has no rule that makes a promise on one product depend on the state of another. Product order is rule text only.

scenarios.title: Promises below the household minimum are not recorded
scenarios.known_gap: Limits are per product. The schema has no limit across products, so a minimum on the sum of all promises is rule text only.

scenarios.title: A dispute outranks a promise at the close
scenarios.known_gap: close.forced can test "a promise was recorded" and "notes without any promise", but not "some product has a note with this reason". The promise rule fires first.

scenarios.title: A confirmed promise may still be recorded after a transfer to plans
scenarios.known_gap: promise.forbidden_after_transfer is one switch for every queue. An exception for one queue cannot be written, and the reference spec keeps the general rule.
